intro.title: Rainwater harvester: tank, autonomy and savings
intro.body: WaterPulse is a free calculator to size a rainwater harvester. Enter your location, roof area and uses (garden, vegetable patch, toilet, laundry) to estimate collectable water, save water and improve water autonomy — useful for an off-grid home, self-sufficiency or drought resilience. The recommended tank volume covers about 21 days of reserve.

how.title: How to size a rainwater tank?
how.lead: In a few steps, get a clear estimate for water autonomy, irrigation or a DIY home project.

steps.title: 1. Locate your roof
steps.body: Pick a country and city, or use the map and GPS. WaterPulse fetches average yearly rainfall (mm) via Open-Meteo to estimate your roof potential.

steps.title: 2. Describe roof and uses
steps.body: Enter roof area in m², roof type (tiles, flat, metal), household size and uses: garden, vegetable patch / irrigation, toilet, laundry — to save more water day to day.

steps.title: 3. Review tank and autonomy
steps.body: The calculator shows collectable water, needs, recommended tank volume and an indicative water autonomy percentage toward greater self-sufficiency.

faq.title: Frequently asked questions
faq.lead: Short answers to get the most from this rainwater harvester calculator.

items.question: How is collectable water calculated?
items.answer: Collectable water (L/year) = roof area (m²) × rainfall (mm) × roof coefficient × 0.9 (filtration). One millimetre on 1 m² equals 1 litre.

items.question: How is tank volume chosen?
items.answer: The recommended tank volume is about 21 days of reserve based on the minimum of collectable water and yearly needs, then rounded to a common size — useful for a DIY guide or installer quote.

items.question: Is rainwater potable / drinking water?
items.answer: Collected rainwater is generally not potable without proper treatment. WaterPulse mainly sizes non-potable uses (garden, vegetable patch, automatic irrigation, toilet, laundry). For drinking water or an off-grid home, have the system validated by a professional.

items.question: Does this help with drought?
items.answer: Indicatively yes: storing rainwater improves resilience and water autonomy in dry periods, without replacing a full local study.

items.question: Where does rainfall data come from?
items.answer: Averages are derived from the Open-Meteo Archive API (multi-year history) for your latitude and longitude.

items.question: Do results replace a professional study?
items.answer: No. WaterPulse provides an estimate to prepare a self-sufficiency or harvester project. A site survey remains necessary for a final design.
